style.vernacular: Dense Pest street blocks of four- to five-storey Historicist (eclectic, neo-Renaissance, Secession) apartment houses in cream, ochre and grey-beige render with rusticated ground floors, window pediments and wrought-iron balconies, built around inner courtyards with gallery access balconies. Buda hillsides carry lower villas and church towers under clay-tile hip roofs. Socialist-era grey and pastel prefabricated panel estates (panelhaz) of 4 to 10 storeys dominate the outer districts, with low glass-and-render retail boxes and pavilion hospitals from the 1890s to 1970s on the fringes. Plane, linden and chestnut street trees.
style.ornament: Neo-Renaissance and eclectic window surrounds with triangular and segmental pediments, rusticated ground floors, wrought-iron balcony railings, carved gateways into courtyards, Secession floral relief and Zsolnay glazed roof tiles on landmark buildings, copper-roofed corner turrets, Baroque whitewashed village churches with red window bands, and prefab concrete panel walls with pastel paint on estates.

sources.what: historic centre listed for classical monuments (Matthias Church, Buda Castle, Parliament, Opera, Basilica); communist-era gutting of Buda Castle
